subject: Proposal: Tiered performance credits + price-hold for renewal
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@medifox.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: MediFox Procurement <procurement@medifox.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — pricing protections + performance credits

Neha,

We’re starting our internal review for the upcoming renewal and want to align on three things before procurement opens the formal RFQ next week:

- A time-limited price-hold on our current committed rate (we’d prefer 9–12 months) while we pilot a larger feature rollout.
- Performance credits tied to tail-latency or token-cost spikes during peak windows — we saw a handful of incidents last quarter where latency impacted user flows and want a mechanism to offset that.
- Flexibility to step up commit mid-term without penalty and a clear onboarding credit for new capacity.

Our target timeline: get a commercial framework this week so procurement can route it to legal by Friday. Can you outline a proposal, including how credits would trigger (SLO thresholds) and the mechanics for a mid-term commit increase?

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director of Platform
MediFox
[julia@medifox.com]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@medifox.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — pricing protections + performance credits

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely put together a commercial framework that hits those three points and keeps the path to a faster legal review. High level thoughts:

- Price-hold: we can offer a 12-month hold at current committed rate, or shorten to 9 months with an onboarding credit if you prefer the shorter horizon.
- Performance credits: suggest a tiered credit ladder tied to 95th/99th percentile latency breaches and a separate cap for burst-token surges.
- Mid-term commit increases: allow step-ups with a pro-rated onboarding credit and an adjusted commit floor; provide a one-time true-up on month-end.

I’ve looped in Karthik (pricing) and Vanessa (Customer Success) to draft the concrete numbers. We’ll attach an initial pricing grid and a draft SOW for your review within 24 hours.

Next steps: Karthik will send a proposal matrix; Vanessa can outline operational triggers for credits. If procurement wants a single document, we’ll prepare an SOW+exhibit.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[neha_kapoor@redwood.com]
[Attachment: Pricing_Grid.csv (csv)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing matrix for MediFox renewal (draft)

Team — draft numbers below (sending to Julia after internal alignment):

Proposal summary:
1) Price-hold option A: 12 months at existing committed unit price (no CPI escalator).
2) Price-hold option B: 9 months at existing price + onboarding credit of $25k if MediFox ups commit by >= $200k ARR.

Performance-credit ladder (applies monthly, capped at 10% of monthly invoice):
- Tier 1 (minor breach): 95th percentile latency > 350ms for > 6 hours in a rolling 30-day window => 2% credit.
- Tier 2 (material breach): 95th percentile latency > 500ms for > 3 hours => 5% credit + operational remediation pledge.
- Tier 3 (severe): 99th percentile latency spike > 1s across > 1 hour => 10% credit + optional canary rollback to previous model variant.

Burst-token protection: monthly cap on overage token charges for burst days (first 3 burst days/month reimbursed as credits up to $15k).

Commit increase mechanics:
- Step-up permitted once per quarter; new commit becomes effective next billing period and onboarding credit is pro-rated.
- True-up aligns at month-end; any under-delivery on original commit triggers standard reconciliation.

Open items for legal: precise SLO measurement (metric definitions + telemetry hook), credit offset mechanics (invoice credit vs. cash refund), and DocuSign exhibit wording.

Attaching the pricing grid and an SOW stub for illustration. If we agree internally, Neha — we can send this as a single package to Julia and procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Pricing_Grid.csv (csv)]
From: Julia Park <julia@medifox.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: MediFox Procurement <procurement@medifox.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing matrix for MediFox renewal (draft)

Neha / Karthik — thanks for the quick draft. A few items from our side:

- We prefer option B (9 months + onboarding credit) if the onboarding credit is guaranteed upon commit increase. Given our internal budgeting, a 9-month horizon is easier for our projections.
- Can you make the performance-credit triggers a little more conservative on the 95th/99th thresholds? A 350ms 95th feels low given our real-world traffic; would you accept 500ms/1s as Tier 1/3 anchors?
- For burst protection, instead of a per-month reimbursed cap, can we convert the first three burst days into a one-time credit that flows at renewal if unused? That helps us preserve runway.

Procurement is also asking for a target DocuSign timeline — we need the final SOW + exhibit by next Wednesday to give legal time. If you can commit to that, procurement will prioritize review.

CC’ing procurement (procurement@medifox.com) — they’ll add any mandatory clauses.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director of Platform, MediFox
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@medifox.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, MediFox Procurement <procurement@medifox.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final: 9-month price-hold + onboarding credit — confirmation and next steps

Julia / team — we appreciate the feedback and can confirm the revised commercial framework you requested:

1) Price-hold: 9 months at current committed rate (Option B).
2) Onboarding credit: $25,000 one-time credit applied when MediFox increases committed annual spend by >= $200,000 (net-new capacity) within the first 90 days of the new term. Credit will appear as an invoice credit within the first billing cycle after the step-up.
3) Performance-credit thresholds: adjusted per your ask —
   - Tier 1: 95th percentile latency > 500ms for > 6 hours in a 30-day window => 2% monthly credit.
   - Tier 2: 95th percentile latency > 750ms for > 3 hours => 5% monthly credit + a remediation plan.
   - Tier 3: 99th percentile latency > 1s for > 1 hour => 10% monthly credit + rollback option.
4) Burst protection: first three burst days per rolling 12-month term convert to a one-time credit at renewal if unused (credit calculation per Pricing_Grid.csv).

Next steps:
- We will bundle the SOW + Exhibit A (credit mechanics) and send a DocuSign package to procurement by Monday EOD.
- Legal redlines should be routed to redwood-legal@redwood.com with the HubSpot deal ID (RDW-6783) in the subject.
- Schedule: I’ve proposed a 30-minute sync for Tuesday to confirm operational hooks (I’ll send the calendar invite).

Attachments: MediFox_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW draft), Pricing_Grid.csv (credit math).

If procurement needs an accelerated DocuSign link now, let me know and I’ll prioritize. Thanks — looking forward to closing this so we can support your launch.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
[Attachment: MediFox_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), Pricing_Grid.csv (csv)]
